text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Tobacco authority has worked out programme to boost output and give incentives to tobacco growers.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Farmers in Constanta county planted kiwi four years ago and now small crop is ready for harvest.
AZI
- SNCFR railway authority plans 20-year concessions of railway sectors.
LIBERTATEA
- Asigurarea Romaneasca SA Romanian insurer plans to raise share capital to 60 billion lei through contribution from strategic investor.
General:
All newspapers report on signing ceremony of long-delayed Romanian-Hungarian treaty due on Monday in western city of Timisoara.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Nicolae Manolescu, National Liberal Alliance (ANL) presidential candidate, said ANL would join coalition government with opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) and Social Democratic Union (USD) after the November 3 polls.
- By the year 2020 Romania's population will drop by up to two million from present level, said national statistics board.
- One-page report on late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu's visit to Moscow on December 4, 1989, days before he was ousted and shot in popular uprising.
ADEVARUL
- Editorial says Romanian-Hungarian treaty would help Budapest join NATO, while Bucharest gets only congratulations.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanian-Hungarian treaty, to be signed today in western city of Timisoara, gives guarantees on borders, says Foreign Ministr Teodor Melescanu in interview.
- Candidacy of President Ion Iliescu for a new term is seen as unsuitable by 50 percent of people polled at end-August.
- Newspaper runs agenda of seven contenders in the race for the November 3 presidential polls.
ZIUA
- Adrian Severin, deputy leader of opposition Democratic Party (PD) says Romanian-Hungarian treaty, whose signing is victory of democrats in both countries, is Budapest's passport to NATO membership.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Newspaper publishes text of political treaty with Hungary and chronology of the negotiations.
- Corneliu Vadim Tudor, head of anti-Semitic Greater Romania Party (PRM) registers candidacy for presidency with the Central Electoral Bureau. ($=3,196 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
